storyNotes.originalText: During the famine, Jacob sent ten of his sons to buy GRAIN in Egypt. He kept Benjamin home.
storyNotes.cleanText: During the famine, Jacob sent ten sons to buy grain in Egypt. Benjamin stayed home.

storyNotes.originalText: The brothers bowed before Joseph. They didn’t recognize him, so he pretended to be a STRANGER.
storyNotes.cleanText: The brothers bowed before Joseph without recognizing him. Joseph pretended to be a stranger.

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph said, "You are SPIES!" He kept the brothers under guard for three days.
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph said the brothers were spies and kept them in prison for three days.

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph said, "One of you must stay BEHIND. The rest must bring your brother back to me."
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph kept one brother behind and told the others to bring Benjamin back.

storyNotes.originalText: The brothers said, "God is PUNISHING us for hurting Joseph." When Joseph heard this, he cried.
storyNotes.cleanText: The brothers said God was punishing them for hurting Joseph, and Joseph cried.

storyNotes.originalText: They returned to tell their father what happened. They all found their MONEY in their bags.
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph’s brothers returned home and found their money in their sacks.

storyNotes.originalText: Jacob refused to let the brothers take BENJAMIN back to Egypt.
storyNotes.cleanText: Jacob refused to let Benjamin go back to Egypt with his brothers.

facts.statement: Jacob sent ten of his sons to Egypt to buy grain.
Benjamin went with his brothers on their first trip to Egypt.
The brothers bowed down when they stood before Joseph.
Joseph didn’t recognize his brothers, but they recognized him.
Joseph accused his brothers of being spies.
Joseph kept all of his brothers in prison for seven days.
Joseph told his brothers to come back with Benjamin.
Joseph sent all ten brothers home together.
The brothers thought God was punishing them because of what they had done to Joseph.
Joseph laughed when he heard the brothers talk about hurting him.
Joseph kept Benjamin in prison while the others went home.
Joseph had the brothers’ money put back into their grain sacks.
Jacob was happy to send Benjamin back to Egypt right away.
Simeon stayed in Egypt while the other brothers went home.

clues.text: I sold grain in Egypt and knew my brothers even though they did not know me.
I sent ten of my sons to buy grain but kept Benjamin at home.
I stayed home because my father worried that I would be hurt.
I was the brother kept in Egypt when the others went home.

theologicalApplications.text: Joseph tested his brothers to find out whether they had changed, not to get revenge.
When the brothers felt sorry about hurting Joseph, he cried.
Jesus teaches his people to love enemies and do good to them.
The lesson encourages children to forgive rather than seek revenge.
